title: IBKR-scanner breadth snapshot concurrent-insert fix — non-blocking findings from PR #242's review
description: Non-blocking findings from pr-reviewer's review of PR #242 (backend-market-breadth-indicators-followups), tracked here per CLAUDE.md's autonomous-pipeline rule so they aren't lost once that PR merges. Both concern record_ibkr_breadth_snapshot's new `except (IntegrityError, OperationalError)` concurrent-insert fallback in app/api/routers/ibkr.py.

checklist.step: The `except (IntegrityError, OperationalError)` branch's fallback (`winner = db.get(...)`, `assert winner is not None`) assumes any caught `OperationalError` implies a same-key winner committed and is now readable. That's verified true for `IntegrityError` (IBKRBreadthSnapshotORM's only constraint is the composite PK), but SQLite's whole-file write locking (no WAL/busy_timeout, per app/db/session.py) can raise 'database is locked' `OperationalError` from *any* concurrent write anywhere in the file, not only a race on this exact (series_key, snapshot_date) -- in which case `db.get(...)` legitimately returns None and the assert raises AssertionError instead of the graceful fallback the decision describes. Not a behavior regression (pre-fix, an uncaught OperationalError also propagated to a generic 500), but the fallback logs a misleading 'falling back to the concurrently-committed row' warning for a case where no such row exists, and the new decision entry doesn't carry forward the OperationalError-scope caveat app/data/cache.py's own `_upsert` comment makes for the identical exception pair (see docs/tasks/done/data-cache-followups-followups.json's review comment on PR #56, which reviewed and explicitly accepted this exact scope gap as non-blocking for the same race pattern). Worth either narrowing the assumption (return a clean error/None-safe path when no winner row is actually found) or adding the same explicit scope-limitation comment cache.py's OperationalError branch has.

The `assert winner is not None` at app/api/routers/ibkr.py:359 is a bare `assert`, which is fragile under `python -O`/`PYTHONOPTIMIZE` (assertions compiled out) -- in the scenario above, that would silently turn the failure into `row = None` and a later `AttributeError` on `row.count` instead of even the (still-uninformative but at least present) `AssertionError`. Not a live concern today (no evidence anywhere in the repo of running with `-O`), but worth an explicit `if winner is None: raise ...` guard instead of `assert` if this pattern is reused elsewhere, or at minimum a comment noting the reliance on assertions being enabled.

decisions.decision: Both findings fixed together by narrowing the fallback's assumption (checklist item 1's first option), rather than just adding the scope-limitation comment cache.py's OperationalError branch has (its other, weaker option): the bare `assert winner is not None` at app/api/routers/ibkr.py:359 was replaced with an explicit `if winner is None:` branch that logs a distinct warning (making clear this wasn't actually a same-key race, just an unrelated SQLite lock) and raises `HTTPException(status_code=503, detail=...)` instead of falling through to `row = winner`. The commit's `except (IntegrityError, OperationalError)` comment block was extended with the same IntegrityError-verified-narrow / OperationalError-wider-causes distinction app/data/cache.py's `_upsert` OperationalError branch documents, adapted to explain why this route (unlike `_upsert`) can't just silently discard the failed write. The route's existing `503` `responses={}` entry and docstring paragraph were both updated to describe this second `503` cause alongside the pre-existing transient-scanner-call-failure one, and `backend/openapi.json` (plus the generated `frontend/src/api/types.ts`) were regenerated to match.
decisions.rationale: Rejected the weaker option (leaving the bare `assert` and just adding a comment) because it wouldn't actually fix finding 2 (the `python -O`/`PYTHONOPTIMIZE`-fragility of a bare `assert`), and item 1's own narrower-assumption path already requires distinguishing the 'no winner found' case from the normal fallback anyway -- once that branch exists, turning it into a clean `if/raise` costs nothing extra and directly addresses both findings with one change, rather than leaving finding 2's fragility in place and documenting it as merely acceptable. Chose `HTTPException(503)` over inventing a new response shape because this route already declares and raises `503` for its other transient failure mode (`_resolve_scanner_unavailable`'s disagreeing-gateway-state case) -- reusing the same status code and `ErrorDetail` response model for another genuinely transient, retry-safe failure keeps the route's error surface consistent rather than adding a third distinct failure representation. Rejected retrying the commit internally (re-attempting `db.commit()` a bounded number of times before giving up) as disproportionate for a rare, low-frequency, manually-triggered endpoint -- consistent with `backend-market-breadth-indicators-followups`' own rejection of a locking mechanism (BEGIN IMMEDIATE / app-level mutex) for the same race pattern, and orthogonal to what this task's two findings actually asked for (a misleading log message and a fragile assert, not the absence of a retry). Verified with a new test (`test_operational_error_with_no_same_key_winner_returns_503`) that forces `db.commit()` to raise a real `sqlalchemy.exc.OperationalError` with no concurrent winner ever appearing for the same key, asserting a `503` response (not an uncaught `AssertionError`/500) and that nothing is persisted; the existing `test_concurrent_first_population_falls_back_to_winners_row` (the genuine-same-key-race path) continues to pass unchanged, confirming the narrowed branch doesn't regress the original fallback behavior.

decisions.decision: Addressed pr-reviewer's needs_work finding on PR #283 (raw SQLAlchemy exception leaked into the new 503's client-facing `detail`) by dropping `({type(exc).__name__}: {exc})` from the `HTTPException(status_code=503, ...)` `detail` string entirely, leaving only the app-defined 'Transient write conflict recording breadth snapshot for series_key=...; retry.' message. The preceding `logger.warning(...)` call, which does interpolate `type(exc).__name__`/`exc`, was left untouched -- logging the real exception server-side is fine and matches `app/data/cache.py`'s identical pattern; only the HTTP response body was the problem.
decisions.rationale: This is a straightforward fix of a correctly-identified information-disclosure regression (str() of a real SQLAlchemy OperationalError/IntegrityError embeds the interpolated SQL statement, bound parameters, and a sqlalche.me docs link), not a judgment call with alternatives to weigh. No test changes were needed: `test_operational_error_with_no_same_key_winner_returns_503` only asserts `"nh" in response.json()["detail"]` (the series_key, still present in the generic message), not the exception-derived suffix that was removed, so it continues to pass unchanged. Re-ran `pytest tests/integration/test_ibkr_breadth.py` (17 passed) and the full backend suite (`pytest --cov=app`, 1203 passed, 100% line/branch coverage) plus `ruff check`/`mypy app` (both clean) to confirm no regression.

comments.summary: The new 503's `detail` interpolates the raw SQLAlchemy exception (`{exc}`) directly into the client-facing HTTP response. For a real `OperationalError`/`IntegrityError`, `str(exc)` includes the interpolated SQL statement, the bound parameter dict, and a link to SQLAlchemy's own error-code docs page (verified directly: `str(OperationalError(stmt, params, orig))` reproduces the `[SQL: ...]`/`[parameters: ...]` sections). This regresses this same file's own established convention: the file's other 503 (`_resolve_scanner_unavailable`, line 137) only ever surfaces an app-defined `IBKRUnavailableError` message built entirely from this app's own code, never a raw third-party DB-driver exception with embedded table/column/statement internals; `app/data/cache.py`'s identical `except (IntegrityError, OperationalError)` branch (the very comment this PR's new code cites) only ever logs `exc`, never returns it to the client. Fix: keep the `logger.warning` call (already correct, matches `cache.py`) but drop `{exc}` from the client-facing `detail` string.

review.notes: Full review performed: backend pytest+coverage (1203 passed, 100% line/branch coverage), frontend vitest+coverage (825 passed, 99.7%+), backend ruff+mypy clean, frontend eslint+tsc clean, profit-target stale-wording guard clean, code-review skill pass, and the persisted Playwright e2e suite (make e2e, 22/22 passed, including watchlist.spec.ts's specs which exercise POST /api/ibkr/breadth/snapshot -- the exact touched route -- on its golden path in a real browser; Playwright MCP interactive tools were not available in this session, so the e2e regression suite plus the added unit test covering the actual edge case -- which needs DB-level fault injection, not reproducible by clicking -- served as the practical substitute for an interactive walkthrough). Confirmed backend/openapi.json and frontend/src/api/types.ts reproduce byte-for-byte after regenerating locally -- the claimed description-only diff checks out. The new test test_operational_error_with_no_same_key_winner_returns_503 correctly forces a real OperationalError with no winner ever committed, and is correctly distinguished from the unchanged genuine-race test. The decisions entry adequately explains the narrow+explicit-raise choice. The one blocking finding is the response-detail internals leak above; no non-blocking findings this round (nothing to track as a follow-up task).
